references.text: Abraham's servant asked that the right woman would offer to water his camels. Verse 20 shows the exact fulfillment of this sign, as Rebekah hurriedly drew water for all the camels.
Rebekah begins to fulfill the sign by giving the servant a drink and offering to draw water also for the camels. Verse 20 describes the actual carrying out of this promise.
The servant recounts the event to Rebekah's family, including that she emptied her jar into the trough and drew water for all the camels, confirming God's guidance.
Rachel comes to the well with her father's sheep, and Jacob meets her there. This is a parallel well-meeting scene as in the story of Rebekah, a recurring motif in Genesis.
Zipporah and her sisters come to the well to water their father's sheep. Moses helps them, in yet another well-meeting scene that follows the pattern from Rebekah's story.
The capable woman in Proverbs is described as diligent and hardworking - qualities Rebekah demonstrates as she hurries to draw water for all the camels.
The verses are complementary accounts of the same event (third-person observation versus first-person testimony) that together highlight Rebekah's initiative and hospitality.
